theme: 3 terms on memory safety: the overall guarantee, the rule against two changes at once, and the type that skips the checks

terms.definition: A guarantee that code never reads or writes memory in a way that can corrupt it, like reading past the end of an array.
terms.example: Swift stops on a bad index because of Memory Safety, instead of reading garbage.

terms.definition: A rule that a variable can't be changed by one piece of code while another piece is still using it.
terms.example: Passing `total` twice as `inout` breaks Exclusive Access.

terms.definition: A type that points straight at a memory address, with none of Swift's usual safety checks.
terms.example: The C library wants an UnsafePointer, so wrap it in `withUnsafePointer`.
terms.code:
let value = 42
withUnsafePointer(to: value) { p in
    print(p.pointee)
}

quizzes.question: What type points straight at memory, with none of Swift's usual checks?

video.title: Memory Safety, Exclusive Access & UnsafePointer | Day 52
video.description:
Learn to explain memory safety in Swift: Memory Safety, Exclusive Access & UnsafePointer, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Memory Safety - A guarantee that code never reads or writes memory in a way that can corrupt it, like reading past the end of an array.
Exclusive Access - A rule that a variable can't be changed by one piece of code while another piece is still using it.
UnsafePointer - A type that points straight at a memory address, with none of Swift's usual safety checks.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

Explain Memory Safety, Exclusive Access & UnsafePointer in Swift by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
메모리 안전성, 배타적 접근, UnsafePointer 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Memory Safety - A guarantee that code never reads or writes memory in a way that can corrupt it, like reading past the end of an array.
한국어: 메모리 안전성: 배열 끝을 넘어 읽는 것처럼 메모리를 망가뜨리는 방식으로 읽거나 쓰지 않는다는 보장

Exclusive Access - A rule that a variable can't be changed by one piece of code while another piece is still using it.
한국어: 배타적 접근: 한 코드가 변수를 아직 쓰는 동안 다른 코드가 그 변수를 바꿀 수 없다는 규칙

UnsafePointer - A type that points straight at a memory address, with none of Swift's usual safety checks.
한국어: UnsafePointer: Swift의 평소 안전 검사 없이 메모리 주소를 직접 가리키는 타입

In this video, Mina and Jake sort out why passing one variable twice does not compile, what Swift protects and when unsafe code makes sense, in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.

landscape.hook: Can you explain memory safety in English?

dialogue.title: Same variable twice?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, `move(&coins, &coins)` doesn't compile. It says `inout` arguments can't alias each other.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That breaks Exclusive Access. Two `inout` parameters can't touch `coins` at once.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: But it's the same variable. Why is that dangerous?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: One parameter would change `coins` while the other is still using it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So Exclusive Access protects Memory Safety?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. Memory Safety means code never reads half-changed memory.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And Swift checks all of that for me?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Mostly. But an UnsafePointer skips those checks.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: When would I ever use an UnsafePointer?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Only for C libraries or rare speed tricks. For `coins` and `bank`, stay safe.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. Keep Memory Safety, respect Exclusive Access, and avoid UnsafePointer.
Memory Safety: a crash is better than corrupted data.
